# GEO report: orchard-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

This score is read from code, not measured on a live site. The 4 routes are `/`, `/varieties`, `/visit` and `/account`. They are server-rendered Next.js pages, with a robots file, a sitemap, canonicals and titles all in place. Nothing in the code decides a rule in a way I couldn't read. What the code can't show is how your host or CDN treats real crawlers (see "Can't tell from code").

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

Nothing is wrong in the code. The biggest unknown is whether real crawlers get through your host or CDN, which code can't show.

### 1. Confirm real crawlers reach the site
- **Why it matters:** a firewall or CDN can block crawlers even when `robots.txt` allows them.
- **Where:** your host's access log (not in the repo)
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` (`public/robots.txt:1-2`)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 100 whether it comes back clear or not. The code score doesn't cover bot protection, so this is a live and log question.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt`, plain valid directives |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed | Clear | `public/robots.txt:1-3`. Only `GPTBot` and `ClaudeBot` (training crawlers) are blocked, matching `trainingCrawlers: "block"` |
| GEO-014 | Routes are indexable | Clear | 3 of 3 public routes. `/account` is a deliberate noindex (`app/account/page.tsx:1`) |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical | Clear | `app/page.tsx:1`, `app/varieties/page.tsx:1`, `app/visit/page.tsx:1`, all on `https://www.orchard.example` |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Clear | Server components, no client fetching |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Clear | `public/sitemap.xml`, with a `Sitemap:` line at `public/robots.txt:11` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:5` has `lang="en"`. The 3 public pages have a title and description. `/account` is private and left out |
| GEO-016 | Server-rendered links | Clear | `app/layout.tsx:7`, plain `<a href>` to all 3 public pages |
| GEO-017 | No snippet conflict | Clear | Only `data-nosnippet` on the cookie notice (`app/layout.tsx:9`), which is a scoped choice |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read the layout and 4 pages. There are no images or icon-only controls |
| GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | No mobile app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not present, and not scored |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (info only) | Not applicable | Not an app |

## Other problems found

- **A private page is both blocked and noindexed.** `public/robots.txt:3` has `Disallow: /account`, and `app/account/page.tsx:1` has `robots: { index: false, follow: false }`. Crawlers blocked by robots.txt never fetch the page, so they never see the noindex. A search engine could still list the bare URL if another site links to it. Fix: drop the `Disallow` line and let the noindex do the work, if you want the page reliably kept out of results.

## Worth considering

- **`/visit` promises directions that aren't on the page:** `app/visit/page.tsx:1`: `description: 'Opening times and directions.'`. The page only says "Open Thursday to Sunday, April to October." Add the address, a postcode and the directions as text. Hours and address could also be labelled with LocalBusiness structured data.
- **Site identity isn't stated in a machine-readable way:** `app/layout.tsx:1` has only `metadataBase`. Add Organization/WebSite JSON-LD with the name and URL the site already shows.
- **The sitemap has no dates:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-5` has `<loc>` entries and no `<lastmod>`. Add real modification dates, or generate the sitemap with `app/sitemap.ts`.
- **The varieties could each have a page:** `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`: "Over forty varieties, from Ashmead’s Kernel to Worcester Pearmain." Only two are named and none have their own address. Give each variety a page at `/varieties/<name>` and link to it from the list.
- **"Since 1952" and "over forty" have no supporting detail:** `app/page.tsx:4` and `app/varieties/page.tsx:4`. A short history section and a full list of varieties would back these up for readers.
- **Pages link onward very little:** the home page (`app/page.tsx:4`) has no links in its body to `/varieties` or `/visit`. Add contextual links.
- **There are no social tags:** none of the pages set `openGraph`. Add title, description and image so shared links read well.
- **The sitemap is hand-kept:** `public/sitemap.xml` must be edited by hand when pages are added. Next's `app/sitemap.ts` can generate it.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>`, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Status codes and headers:** whether the server returns 200 for the listed URLs, and whether it sets any `X-Robots-Tag` header outside the repo. A live scan with your URL would show this.
- **GEO-003 in production:** the code is server-rendered, but only a live check confirms what the deployed HTML contains.

## Assumptions

- The goal is for AI search tools to find the site, which matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
- `/account` is deliberately private, so I left it out of the metadata and link checks.
- `https://www.orchard.example` is the real origin, as declared in `geo.config.json`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply the `/account` robots cleanup or any "Worth considering" item. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
